categories_checked.note: Student Finance England (full support vs tuition-fee-only, 2026/27 amounts, LLE from Jan 2027), Student Finance Wales, Student Finance NI (nidirect), SAAS Scotland (only 2021 guidance readable: SAAS site is a JS app), EU nationals without EUSS status, Chevening (UK government scholarship).

No student rent subsidy found. Housing Benefit usually excludes full-time students and people whose visa bars public funds (record gb-housing-benefit-students). Student Finance maintenance loans are the main help with rent for eligible students.
IHS reimbursement for full-time EU/EEA/Swiss students with an EHIC who do not work.
16-25 Railcard discount (GB-wide). TfL 18+ Student Oyster: eligibility read, discount value not confirmed. Wales MyTravelPass and Translink yLink (NI) pages could not be opened.
Income tax personal allowance 2026/27; council tax student exemption in England, Scotland, Wales; Northern Ireland domestic rates (no student exemption for private homes).
No subsidy tied to student work found; work rules are in bureaucracy.json.

European Commission Programme Guide lists the UK as a third country associated to Erasmus+; start date and the Turing Scheme's future could not be confirmed on gov.uk (turing-scheme.org.uk had a certificate error).
Scotland free bus travel for under-22s. Nation-level student finance (SAAS, SFW, SFNI) is under state_grant_loan; nation-level council tax/rates under tax.

Only the general scholarship pages of Edinburgh, Glasgow, St Andrews, LSE and the Cambridge Trust could be read (no amounts on them). Oxford, UCL, Imperial, Cardiff, QUB pages returned 403; other catalogue universities not researched (web search budget exhausted).

items.name_local: Student Finance England: Tuition Fee Loan and Maintenance Loan
items.name_it: Student Finance England: prestito tasse + prestito di mantenimento
items.authority: Student Finance England (Student Loans Company / Department for Education)
items.description: Loans for undergraduate tuition fees and living costs, repaid after graduation. Open to EU citizens only in specific residence categories: settled status, Irish citizens, and EEA/Swiss workers (and family) with settled or pre-settled status.

eligibility.residence_requirement: Settled status or Irish citizen: 3 years living in the UK, Channel Islands or Isle of Man before the course, with England as home. EEA/Swiss workers with settled or pre-settled status: 3 years in the UK, EEA, Gibraltar or Switzerland.
eligibility.income_test: Maintenance Loan amount depends on household income
other: EU citizens without EUSS status (arrived after 2020) are not eligible
Pre-settled status without worker status: tuition fee loan only (gb-sfe-tuition-only)

items.amount: 2026/27: Tuition Fee Loan up to £9,790; Maintenance Loan up to £9,118 (with parents), £10,830 (away, outside London), £14,135 (away, London)
items.how_to_apply: Online with Student Finance England; EU applicants use the EU application route and provide proof of status and residence.
items.stackable: Can be combined with university bursaries/scholarships.
items.notes: Amounts are for courses starting before 1 January 2027; later courses fall under Lifelong Learning Entitlement (gb-sfe-lle-2027).

items.name_local: Student Finance England: tuition fees only (EU pre-settled status)
items.name_it: Student Finance England: solo prestito tasse (EU con pre-settled status)
items.authority: Student Finance England (Student Loans Company / Department for Education)
items.description: EU citizens with pre-settled status (or temporary protection under the Withdrawal Agreement) and their family members can get a Tuition Fee Loan but no help with living costs.

eligibility.residence_requirement: Pre-settled status (or pending EUSS application) and 3 years living in the UK, EEA, Switzerland or the overseas territories before the course
other: Irish citizens resident in the UK by 31 December 2020 are also listed in this category
No Maintenance Loan unless you qualify as an EEA/Swiss worker or family member (gb-sfe-full-support)

items.amount: Tuition Fee Loan up to £9,790 (2026/27); no living-cost support
items.how_to_apply: Online with Student Finance England, EU tuition-fee-only application, with proof of EUSS status.

items.name_local: Lifelong Learning Entitlement (courses starting on or after 1 January 2027)
items.name_it: Lifelong Learning Entitlement (corsi che iniziano dal 1 gennaio 2027)
items.authority: Student Finance England / Department for Education
items.description: For most courses in England starting on or after 1 January 2027 student finance is applied for through the Lifelong Learning Entitlement. Settled status holders and Irish citizens with 3 years' UK residence can get tuition and maintenance loans; pre-settled status holders may only get a Tuition Fee Loan.

eligibility.residence_requirement: 3 years in the UK, Channel Islands or Isle of Man before the first day of the month the course starts (settled status / Irish citizens)
other: Courses starting on or after 1 January 2027

items.how_to_apply: Through the Lifelong Learning Entitlement application (Student Finance England).
items.notes: LLE amounts not read; the 2026/27 figures in gb-sfe-full-support apply to courses starting before 1 January 2027.

items.name_local: EU nationals without EUSS status: no home fees or student finance
items.name_it: Cittadini UE senza EUSS status: niente home fees né finanziamenti
items.authority: Student Finance NI / SAAS / Department for Education
items.description: Since courses starting in 2021/22, EU/EEA/Swiss nationals generally lose home fee status and UK student finance unless they have citizens' rights under the Withdrawal Agreement, i.e. settled or pre-settled status. Without it they pay international fees set by each university. Irish citizens are the exception.

other: EU/EEA/Swiss citizens who moved to the UK after 31 December 2020 without EUSS status
Does not apply to Irish citizens

items.notes: Fee status is decided by the university's fee assessor; the international fee level differs per university.

items.name_local: Student Finance Wales: EU students
items.name_it: Student Finance Wales: studenti UE
items.description: For study in Wales, EU citizens with settled or pre-settled status who have lived 3 years in the UK and Islands and live in Wales on the first day of the course can get tuition fee and living-cost support. Others with EUSS status and 3 years in the UK/EEA/Switzerland/overseas territories can get tuition fee support only.

eligibility.residence_requirement: Tuition + living costs: 3 years in the UK and Islands, living in Wales on day one. Tuition only: 3 years in the UK, EEA, Switzerland or overseas territories, studying and living in Wales on day one.
other: Settled or pre-settled status, or a Certificate of Application
Irish citizens do not need EUSS status but must meet the residence tests

items.how_to_apply: Apply to Student Finance Wales.
items.notes: Unlike England, the Welsh page lists pre-settled status (with 3 years' UK residence) for living-cost support too. Amounts not read. Relevant for Cardiff University.

items.name_local: Student Finance NI: EU students
items.name_it: Student Finance NI: studenti UE
items.authority: Student Finance NI (Department for the Economy, Northern Ireland)
items.description: For courses from 2021/22, non-Irish EU/EEA/Swiss nationals need settled or pre-settled status for home fees and Student Finance NI support. Tuition fee help generally needs 3 years' residence in the EEA/Switzerland not mainly for full-time education; living-cost help needs 3 years in the UK and Islands plus migrant worker status (or child of a Swiss national / Turkish worker). Irish citizens keep their rights under the Common Travel Area.

eligibility.residence_requirement: 3 years in the EEA and Switzerland before the course (tuition); 3 years in the UK and Islands (living costs)
other: Settled or pre-settled status required except for Irish citizens
Late EUSS applicants with reasonable grounds may be treated as eligible while the application is pending

items.how_to_apply: Apply to Student Finance NI.
items.notes: Amounts not on the page. Relevant for Queen's University Belfast.

items.name_local: SAAS (Student Awards Agency Scotland): EU students
items.name_it: SAAS (Scozia): studenti UE
items.description: In Scotland, EU nationals living in the UK before the end of 2020 with settled or pre-settled status, 3 years' residence in the UK/EEA/Switzerland and ordinary residence in the UK can get home fee status; SAAS pays Scottish home tuition fees for eligible students. EU nationals who arrived from 2021 without status are charged international fees and get no SAAS funding.

eligibility.residence_requirement: Living in the UK before 31 December 2020, settled or pre-settled status, 3 years in the UK, EEA or Switzerland, ordinarily resident in the UK on the relevant date (1 August for autumn courses)
other: SAAS guidance says pre-settled holders with protected rights but under 3 years in the UK may get tuition fees only

items.how_to_apply: Apply to SAAS online.
items.notes: The only readable SAAS document is the EU Residence Guide updated 6 October 2021 (for 2021-22 starters; home fee then £1,820). The current SAAS pages could not be read, so 2026/27 amounts and any rule changes were not confirmed. Relevant for Edinburgh, Glasgow, Strathclyde, St Andrews.

items.name_local: Chevening Scholarships
items.name_it: Borse Chevening
items.description: UK government scholarship for a one-year master's degree at a UK university. It covers full tuition, a monthly living stipend (London and non-London rates), economy return flights, the visa fee and travel/arrival allowances. Applicants commit to return to their country for at least 2 years.

other: Citizen of a Chevening-eligible country (the eligibility page's country list includes the EU member states; there is a Chevening page for Italy)
Undergraduate degree finished at least 2 years before the deadline
2 years (2,800 hours) of work experience after the degree
Apply to 3 eligible UK courses and hold an unconditional offer by the deadline
Not for British or dual British citizens or people resident in the UK when applying

items.amount: Full tuition + monthly stipend + flights + visa fee (stipend amount not stated)
items.how_to_apply: Online on chevening.org during the application window.
items.deadline: 2027-28 cycle: opened August 2026, closed October 2026 (now closed); next cycle not yet listed
items.notes: EU eligibility is inferred from the country list on the eligibility page, not stated as a rule.

items.name_local: GREAT Scholarships
items.name_it: Borse GREAT
items.authority: British Council / UK government with UK universities
items.description: Scholarships for one-year postgraduate taught courses for students from selected countries. The official page could not be read, so countries, amounts and deadlines were not confirmed.

items.name_local: Housing Benefit (generally not for full-time students)
items.name_it: Housing Benefit (in genere escluso per studenti a tempo pieno)
items.authority: Department for Work and Pensions / local councils
items.description: There is no national rent subsidy for students. Housing Benefit usually cannot be claimed by full-time students, or by people whose visa says they cannot claim public funds.

other: Exclusion applies to full-time students and Student visa holders (no recourse to public funds)

items.notes: gov.uk describes these as usual exclusions, not absolute ones.

items.name_local: Immigration Health Surcharge reimbursement for EU students
items.name_it: Rimborso dell'Immigration Health Surcharge per studenti UE
items.authority: Department of Health and Social Care / NHS Business Services Authority
items.description: Full-time EU/EEA/Swiss students on a Student visa who hold a valid EHIC and do not work can get the IHS refunded, fully or for the period covered by the EHIC (rounded down to 6 months).

eligibility.stay_duration: Visa longer than 6 months, starting on or after 1 January 2021
other: Full-time higher education student (level 4+ in England, Wales, NI; level 7+ in Scotland)
Valid EHIC issued by an EU country, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein or Switzerland, with at least 6 months left when the visa starts
Not working and not intending to work in the UK (paid jobs, paid placements and paid university contracts count as work)

items.amount: Up to the full IHS paid (£776/year for students in 2026)
items.how_to_apply: Online form on gov.uk with IHS number, visa share code, EHIC and CAS scans.
items.deadline: Within 12 months of arriving in the UK
items.stackable: Refund is lost if you work; reimbursements cannot be reversed.
items.notes: The guidance page was last updated February 2024 and gives no closing date.

items.name_local: 16-25 Railcard
items.name_it: 16-25 Railcard
items.description: One third off most rail fares in Great Britain, including Advance tickets. A £12 minimum fare applies Monday to Friday 04:30-09:59.

other: Mature full-time students 26+ with an endorsed form

items.amount: 1/3 off fares; card costs £35/year or £80/3 years (2026)
items.how_to_apply: Buy online at 16-25railcard.co.uk.

items.name_local: 18+ Student Oyster photocard (London)
items.name_it: 18+ Student Oyster photocard (Londra)
items.description: Discounted travel in London for students aged 18+ living in a London borough. The discount percentage and card fee were not shown on the page read.

other: Must be a student; full-time requirement and eligible institutions not confirmed

items.how_to_apply: Apply online through TfL.
items.notes: Only the eligibility sentence could be read on 2026-11-25; check discount and fee on TfL before quoting them.

items.name_local: Income Tax Personal Allowance
items.name_it: Soglia esente da imposta sul reddito (Personal Allowance)
items.description: The first £12,570 of income in the 2026/27 tax year is tax-free; income from £12,571 to £50,270 is taxed at 20% (England, Wales, NI). Scotland has different income tax bands.
items.how_to_apply: Applied automatically through PAYE; tax overpaid can be reclaimed from HMRC.

items.name_local: Council Tax exemption for full-time students (England)
items.name_it: Esenzione Council Tax per studenti a tempo pieno (Inghilterra)
items.description: Households where everyone is a full-time student do not pay Council Tax. If a non-student lives with you, a bill is issued but a discount may apply. Apply to the council for the exemption if you receive a bill.

other: Full-time student: course of at least 1 year with at least 21 hours of study per week
Under 20 on courses up to A level: at least 3 months and 12 hours/week

items.how_to_apply: Apply to your local council with a student status certificate from your university.

items.name_local: Council Tax exemption for full-time students (Scotland)
items.name_it: Esenzione Council Tax per studenti a tempo pieno (Scozia)
items.description: No Council Tax if everyone in the household is a full-time student or if you live in halls of residence. A full-time student living with adults who pay may not have to contribute.

other: Over 20: in higher education, or at least 21 hours/week on a course of at least 24 weeks a year
Under 20: further or higher education, or at least 12 hours/week on a course of at least 3 months

items.amount: 100% exemption for all-student households and halls
items.how_to_apply: Tell your council about your studies when registering for Council Tax.

items.name_local: Council Tax exemption for full-time students (Wales)
items.name_it: Esenzione Council Tax per studenti a tempo pieno (Galles)
items.description: Properties occupied only by full-time students (Class N) and qualifying student halls (Class M) are exempt, including during holidays. A student living with non-students is disregarded, which can give the others a 25% discount.

other: Normally full-time: at least 21 hours/week in term on a course of at least 24 weeks per academic year
Non-British spouses/dependants of international students barred from work/benefits may also be disregarded

items.amount: 100% exemption for all-student properties; 25% discount possible in mixed households
items.how_to_apply: Contact your local authority Council Tax department.

items.name_local: Domestic rates in Northern Ireland (no student exemption for private homes)
items.name_it: Domestic rates in Irlanda del Nord (nessuna esenzione studenti per case private)
items.authority: Land & Property Services / Department of Finance (Northern Ireland)
items.description: Northern Ireland has domestic rates instead of Council Tax. Halls of residence are exempt, but there is no exemption for private homes occupied by full-time students. In a house in multiple occupation (3+ tenants from 2+ families) the landlord is responsible for rates; for other rentals the landlord pays if the capital value is £150,000 or less.
items.notes: The 'no student exemption' statement comes from a Department of Finance FOI response (data as at April 2023), not a guidance page. Relevant for Queen's University Belfast.

items.name_local: Erasmus+ (UK as associated country)
items.name_it: Erasmus+ (Regno Unito come paese associato)
items.description: The Erasmus+ Programme Guide now lists the United Kingdom as a third country associated to the programme, subject to the association agreement. Incoming exchange students' Erasmus+ grant is paid by their home institution/country.

other: Exchange must be between institutions taking part in Erasmus+
From which academic year UK universities run Erasmus+ exchanges again was not confirmed

items.how_to_apply: Through your home university's international office.
items.notes: Verified: the EC page lists the UK as associated, citing Council Decision (EU) 2026/833 of 30 March 2026. Not verified: the start year (not stated on the page; the EUR-Lex text and gov.uk announcements could not be read) and whether UK hosts add anything for incoming students.

items.name_local: Turing Scheme
items.name_it: Turing Scheme
items.description: UK government scheme that funds outgoing study and work placements abroad for students of UK institutions. It funds outgoing students only and does not fund incoming students.

other: Students enrolled at a UK institution going abroad

items.how_to_apply: Through the UK university, which applies for the funding.
items.notes: Official site could not be read (TLS certificate error on 2026-11-25). Its current funding year and whether it continues alongside Erasmus+ were not confirmed.

items.name_local: Young Persons' (Under 22s) Free Bus Travel Scheme
items.name_it: Bus gratis under 22 in Scozia
items.description: Free bus travel in Scotland for people aged 5-21 who live in Scotland, with a National Entitlement Card.

other: The page does not say whether international/EU students living in Scotland during their studies qualify

items.how_to_apply: Online at getyournec.scot or through the local council, with ID, proof of address and a photo.
items.notes: Relevant for Edinburgh, Glasgow, Strathclyde, St Andrews.

items.name_local: University of Edinburgh: scholarships for international and EU undergraduates
items.name_it: University of Edinburgh: borse per studenti internazionali e UE
items.description: Edinburgh lists scholarships for international/EU undergraduates, including Global Talent Fund BIG Scholarships, Edinburgh Global Undergraduate Maths Scholarships, a Vet School international scholarship and an Asylum Seeker Scholarship. Amounts and criteria are on each scholarship page.

other: Usually international (overseas) fee status

items.how_to_apply: See each scholarship page / the university scholarship search.
items.notes: Only the list of names was verified, not amounts or deadlines.

items.name_local: University of Glasgow: World Changers Glasgow Scholarships
items.name_it: University of Glasgow: World Changers Glasgow Scholarships
items.description: Glasgow says it has allocated over £15 million to international scholarships (World Changers Glasgow Scholarships) based on academic excellence. Individual amounts and deadlines are on the undergraduate/postgraduate fees and funding pages.

other: International fee status

items.how_to_apply: See the university's fees and funding pages.

items.name_local: University of St Andrews: undergraduate scholarships
items.name_it: University of St Andrews: borse per undergraduate
items.description: St Andrews offers awards that cover all or part of international tuition fees or accommodation costs, depending on programme, country of residence, household income, achievements and fee status. Applications can be made before receiving an offer.

eligibility.income_test: Some awards are means-tested on household income

items.how_to_apply: Search the scholarships catalogue and apply; contact ugscholarships@st-andrews.ac.uk.

items.name_local: LSE: financial support for Overseas fee status students
items.name_it: LSE: aiuti per studenti con Overseas fee status
items.authority: London School of Economics and Political Science
items.description: LSE offers donor-funded bursaries and scholarships to Overseas fee status undergraduates; their number, value and criteria change each year. The LSE Bursary and Accommodation Bursary are only for Home fee status students or UK nationals.

other: Overseas fee status

items.how_to_apply: See LSE's Overseas financial support page / Financial Support Office.

items.name_local: Cambridge Trust scholarships
items.name_it: Borse Cambridge Trust
items.description: The Cambridge Trust funds undergraduate and postgraduate scholarships for students with outstanding academic potential at the University of Cambridge, with a 'find a scholarship' tool by eligibility.
items.how_to_apply: See cambridgetrust.org (undergraduate / postgraduate applicants).
items.notes: Amounts, deadlines and application process not on the page read.
